# Adjudication Task — Chapter 194

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃194화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“아따, 시원하다.”
  6|
  7|잠시 소피를 보고 온다던 적천강이 돌아온 것은 일각이 지난 후였다. 어쩐지 수상쩍은 느낌에 나는 눈을 가늘게 떴다.
  8|
  9|“눈을 왜 그따위로 뜨느냐?”
 10|
 11|“정말 소피보고 오신 거 맞아요?”
 12|
 13|“냄새라도 맡아 봐야 믿겠느냐?”
 14|
 15|“일각이나 걸리셨는데. 혹시.”
 16|
 17|“노부가 한 정력 하느니라.”
 18|
 19|“…….”
 20|
 21|대체 얼마나 정력이 좋으면 소변을 15분이나 보는 거야.
 22|
 23|그 정도면 소변이 아니라 소방 호스 아닌가. 내가 어이없단 표정으로 바라보자 적천강이 눈을 치켜떴다.
 24|
 25|“뭐, 불만 있어?”
 26|
 27|“그럴 리가요.”
 28|
 29|불만이라니.
 30|
 31|오늘 그에게 받은 도움을 생각하면 백 번을 절해도 부족하다.
 32|
 33|‘그리고 또…….’
 34|
 35|문득 떠오르는 생각을 흩어 버렸다.
 36|
 37|열화문의 신물, 화왕의 제자. 아까부터 끊임없이 수군거리는 목소리들도 애써 못 들은 척했다.
 38|
 39|‘제자라니, 말도 안 되는 소리.’
 40|
 41|지금까지 단 한 번도 생각해 본 적 없는 문제였다.
 42|
 43|애초에 만난 지 하루 된, 그것도 자식처럼 끔찍이 아끼던 제자를 죽인 놈을 새로운 제자로 받아들일 이유가 어디 있겠는가.
 44|
 45|‘비록 그 제자가 천하의 개썅놈이라도 말이지.’
 46|
 47|그런 생각을 하고 있을 때, 진위경이 다가와 적천강에게 지극히 공손한 태도로 포권을 취했다.
 48|
 49|“무림 말학 진위경이 천하에 위명이 자자하신 화왕 적천강 대협을 뵙습니다.”
 50|
 51|“진가?”
 52|
 53|진위경을 위아래로 스캔한 적천강이 감 잡았다는 듯 고개를 끄덕였다.
 54|
 55|“하면 자네가 이놈 애비 되는 사람인가?”
 56|
 57|“예?”
 58|
 59|“자식 교육 좀 똑바로 시키게. 어린놈이 벌써부터 욱해서 사고나 치고 다니고 말이야. 말투도 영 싸가지가 없어.”
 60|
 61|진위경이 지금까지 본 가장 어두운 얼굴로 대답했다.
 62|
 63|“……제 아우입니다.”
 64|
 65|“응?”
 66|
 67|“제가 태경이 큰형 되는 사람입니다.”
 68|
 69|적천강이 정색했다.
 70|
 71|“농담하지 말게. 젊어 보이고 싶은 마음은 알지만 욕심이 너무 과하면 천벌 받아.”
 72|
 73|“사실입니다. 태원진가의 소가주 진위경이 바로 접니다.”
 74|
 75|“……혹시 나이가 어떻게 되나?”
 76|
 77|“해가 바뀌었으니 올해로 서른여섯입니다.”
 78|
 79|적천강이 불신의 눈빛으로 중얼거렸다.
 80|
 81|“마흔 여섯은 되어 보이는데.”
 82|
 83|나이에 비해 좀, 상당히, 많이 삭은 얼굴이긴 하지. 처음에는 나도 아버지로 착각했을 정도니까.
 84|
 85|그나마 머리카락은 풍성한데, 세월을 160km 패스트볼로 맞은 얼굴은 해결책이 안 보인다.
 86|
 87|슬픔에 잠긴 진위경의 표정에 적천강이 애써 위로했다.
 88|
 89|“괜찮아. 사내는 능력일세. 예쁜 색시에 귀여운 자식 놈들이 있으니 됐지 뭘. 허허.”
 90|
 91|“아직 홀몸입니다.”
 92|
 93|“……서른여섯인데?”
 94|
 95|현대에서야 슬슬 결혼 생각할 나이지만 조혼(早婚)이 흔한 무림에서는 서른여섯이면 손자도 볼 수 있는 나이다.
 96|
 97|싱글남 진위경이 짧게 대답했다.
 98|
 99|“예.”
100|
101|“…….”
102|
103|이번 침묵을 좀 길다. 미간을 찡그렸다가, 폈다가. 콧구멍을 벌름거리던 화왕이 한숨을 푹 내쉬었다.
104|
105|“젠장, 술 땡기네.”
106|
107|나는 피식 웃었다. 오늘 같은 잔칫날에 술이 빠져서야 쓰나, 주위에 널리고 널린 게 술이다.
108|
109|“한 잔 드려요?”
110|
111|내 말에 적천강이 눈을 동그랗게 떴다.
112|
113|“이런 되바라진 놈을 봤나. 지금 노부랑 장난하는 것이냐?”
114|
115|“예?”
116|
117|“동이째로 가져오너라.”
118|
119|
120|
121|* * *
122|
123|
124|
125|원래 분위기라는 것은 불씨 같아서, 한 번 꺼지면 다시 타오르기 힘들다. 하지만 종남파의 불청객들이 찬물을 뿌리고 난 후에도 불씨는 죽지 않았다.
126|
127|아니, 화왕이라는 존재로 인해 더욱 거세게 타올랐다.
128|
129|“우와아아아!”
130|
131|“마셔! 마시자고!”
132|
133|“내가 살면서 화왕을 직접 보게 될 줄이야.”
134|
135|“화왕이 당황하면 우화왕 좌화왕!”
136|
137|“…….”
138|
139|누군지는 모르지만 방금 저 새끼가 불씨 꺼트릴 뻔했네.
140|
141|내 눈짓에 대기하고 있던 혁무진이 분위기 살인마를 색출하기 위해 슬그머니 자리를 떴다.
142|
143|그사이 적천강은 수많은 사람의 인사를 받고 있었다.
144|
145|“적 대협! 이렇게 뵙게 되어 일생의 영광입니다!”
146|
147|“추후에 꼭 저희 문파에 들러 주시면…….”
148|
149|“가르침을 내려 주십시오!”
150|
151|말 그대로 인산인해.
152|
153|화왕 적천강이라는 이름은 살아 있는 전설이나 다름없다.
154|
155|더군다나 수십 년간 행적이 묘연한 탓에 대부분의 사람들은 그의 죽음을 공공연한 사실로 받아들이고 있었다.
156|
157|그런데 죽은 줄 알았던 화왕이 나타난 것이다. 중원도, 구화산도 아닌 바로 이곳 산서성의 태원진가에.
158|
159|‘난리가 날 수밖에 없지.’
160|
161|팝의 황제라 불리던 전설적인 가수가 살아 돌아온다면 이 정도일까 싶다.
162|
163|하지만 산서성 현지 팬들의 성원에도 불구하고 마이클 천강은 영 떨떠름한 얼굴이었다.
164|
165|진위경도 그런 낌새를 느꼈는지 전음을 보냈다.
166|
167|- 막내야.
168|
169|괴팍한 성격인 적천강과 그나마 길게 말을 섞을 수 있는 사람은 나와 청풍밖에 없는데, 청풍은 어디로 튈지 모르는 놈이라 결국 내가 메신저 역할을 할 수밖에 없었다.
170|
171|“불편한 곳이라도 있으세요?”
172|
173|“노부의 꼴을 봐라. 네 녀석 같으면 안 불편하겠느냐?”
174|
175|적천강이 옆에 놓인 술동이를 노려봤다. 시간이 꽤 흘렀는데도 얼마 비워지지 않은 상태였다.
176|
177|술을 싫어하는 것이 아니라 그만큼 마실 틈이 부족했던 거다.
178|
179|“염병할. 술 한 잔 마시기가 이렇게 힘들어서야.”
180|
181|다짜고짜 제자로 받아 달라는 사람, 귀빈으로 모시고 싶다는 문주들과 상인들.
182|
183|심지어 어떤 만삭의 여인은 코를 만져 봐도 되냐고 묻기까지 했다. 화왕의 기운을 받아 큰 인물을 낳고 싶다나 뭐라나.
184|
185|‘돌하르방인가.’
186|
187|보는 사람도 실소가 새어 나올 정도인데 당사자는 오죽할까.
188|
189|사실 적천강의 성격에 이 정도 버틴 것만 해도 대단한 거다.
190|
191|“그럼 미리 준비해 둔 곳으로 자리를 옮길까요? 거긴 조용한데.”
192|
193|“끄응. 됐다.”
194|
195|“불편하시다면서요.”
196|
197|“아, 됐다면 된 거지 왜 이렇게 말이 많아?”
198|
199|투덜거리면서도 끝끝내 자리를 뜨지 않는 적천강의 모습에 나는 고개를 갸우뚱했다.
200|
201|‘뭐지?’
202|
203|만난 시간은 짧지만 그의 성격은 어느 정도 알고 있다.
204|
205|시끄러운 곳 싫어하고 사람들의 관심을 귀찮아하는 게 눈에 보일 정도다. 애초에 그런 성격이니 일평생을 구화산에서 살았던 것이고.
206|
207|‘그런데 왜?’
208|
209|나는 유심히 적천강의 모습을 살폈다.
210|
211|그의 앞에는 산서성에서 방귀깨나 뀐다는 상회(商會)의 주인이 허리를 굽실거리고 있었다.
212|
213|“아이고! 적천강 대협! 천하를 떨어 울리는 위명은 익히 들었습니다. 제가 어릴 때 얼마나 대협을…….”
214|
215|“본론만 말하게.”
216|
217|“평소 마음 깊이 대협을 흠모하던 터라 약소한 성의를 준비했습니다.”
218|
219|“약소한 성의?”
220|
221|“예. 얼마 전에 얻은 물건이온데, 역시 주인을 따로 있나 봅니다.”
222|
223|품에서 작은 목함을 꺼낸 상인이 뚜껑을 열었다. 투명한 옥이 박힌 반지가 모습을 드러냈다.
224|
225|“피독지환(避毒指環)입니다.”
226|
227|“제법 귀한 물건이군. 구하기 힘들었을 터인데?”
228|
229|상인이 과장스럽게 손을 내저었다.
230|
231|“적 대협의 존안을 뵙게 되었는데 가격이 문제겠습니까! 은자 천 냥 정도밖에 안 합니다. 헤헤.”
232|
233|저런 반지 하나가 은자 천 냥이라니. 지금까지 태원진가에 들어온 예물 중에서도 손에 꼽는 가격이다.
234|
235|하지만 적천강은 별 감흥 없는 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였다.
236|
237|“뭐, 일단 주니까 고맙게 받지. 어디에서 온 누구라고?”
238|
239|“양천상회를 맡고 있는…….”
240|
241|“양천상회? 양천이면 하북이랑 인접해 있군.”
242|
243|이름을 말하기도 전에 말이 끊겼지만 상인은 황송하다는 듯 고개를 숙였다.
244|
245|“예. 하북팽가와 거래를 트려고 합니다만 쉽지가 않습니다.”
246|
247|이게 상인의 본론이다. 결코 약소하지 않은 약소한 성의를 보이면서까지 적천강을 찾아온 이유.
248|
249|요컨대 하북팽가와의 거래를 도와달라는 청탁인 것이다.
250|
251|“팽가라. 지금 가주가 누구지?”
252|
253|“철혈도(鐵血刀) 팽철영 대협이십니다.”
254|
255|“처음 듣는 이름인데. 벽력도왕(霹靂刀王)의 자식인가?”
256|
257|“예, 예. 벽력도왕께서 일선에서 물러나시며 가주 직을 승계했습니다.”
258|
259|“노부가 소싯적에 벽력도왕이랑 술 한잔했지. 일단 알았네.”
260|
261|이야기는 그것으로 끝이었다. 상인은 입이 찢어져라 웃으며 목함을 내려놓고 사라졌다.
262|
263|목함 아래에는 방금 전까지 안 보이던 전표 다발이 깔려 있었다.
264|
265|나는 상인이 물러난 틈을 타 속삭였다.
266|
267|“벽력도왕과도 아는 사이세요?”
268|
269|별호로 알 수 있듯이, 그 역시 적천강과 같은 십왕(十王)에 속해있는 초절정 고수다.
270|
271|적천강이 술을 홀짝이며 대답했다.
272|
273|“말했잖느냐. 술 한잔했다고.”
274|
275|“우와.”
276|
277|벽력도왕을 무슨 동네 친구 만난 것처럼 얘기하네. 이럴 때마다 새삼 적천강의 대단함을 깨닫게 된다.
278|
279|내가 입을 쩍 벌리고 감탄하자 적천강이 우쭐거렸다.
280|
281|“석년에 그놈 코를 주저앉혀 놨지.”
282|
283|“……예?”
284|
285|“검성이랑 같이 술 한잔하는데 말도 없이 끼어들더니 시비를 걸지 뭐냐. 한 판 붙어서 혼쭐을 내 줬다.”
286|
287|아니, 이게 무슨 소리야.
288|
289|“치, 친구 사이 아니었어요?”
290|
291|“내가? 그놈이랑?”
292|
293|적천강이 눈썹을 찡그렸다.
294|
295|“그런 무식한 놈하고 상종해서 뭐 해. 그 후로 서로 얼굴 볼 일도 없었다.”
296|
297|“…….”
298|
299|“나중에는 별 괴상한 소문까지 돌더군. 노부와 팽가 놈이 백여 초를 겨룬 끝에 서로를 인정하고 물러났다나 뭐라나. 분명 하북팽가 놈들이 수작을 부린 거겠지.”
300|
301|그 말에 나와 주위에 있던 사람들은 기가 막혔다.
302|
303|벽력도왕과의 스토리도 어이가 없지만, 그렇게 되면 앞서 받은 상인의 청탁도 물거품이 되기 때문이다.
304|
305|“그, 그럼 양천상회는 하북팽가와 거래 못 하지 않나요? 적 대협 이름을 대 봤자 역효과만 날 텐데.”
306|
307|적천강이 눈을 깜빡거렸다.
308|
309|“양천상회? 그게 무엇이냐?”
310|
311|“……?”
312|
313|“아아, 방금 그놈? 그걸 왜 내가 신경 써?”
314|
315|“아니, 하북팽가랑 거래할 수 있도록 도와주신다고 하셨잖아요.”
316|
317|“만나 달라고 해서 만나 준 것뿐이다. 벽력도왕이랑 술 마신 것도 사실이고. 노부가 한 말에 일말의 거짓이라도 있느냐?”
318|

“…”

“…”

[P163]
“…”

[P188]
“…”

“From where I’m standing, that doesn’t look like admiration.”

[P194]
“Is that so?”

[P197]
“What?”

[P198]
“I’m saying I’ll give all of it to you.”

[P199]
“All of that?”

[P200]
“It’s completely useless to this old man, but it’s different for you. Scatter it in the street or do whatever you want with it. I won’t care, so take it.”

What was going on?

[P202]
I stared at Jeok Cheongang in bewilderment.

[P203]
*Why all of a sudden?*

[P204]

[P207]

[P208]

[P209]
“Ahh, I’m drunk. I’m going inside to rest. See you tomorrow.”

[P210]
“…”

[P211]
I watched Jeok Cheongang stagger away, then turned my gaze back to the wine crock.

[P212]
The moon was reflected in the wine. He had not even emptied a quarter of the crock.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.

Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

“Ahh, that hit the spot.”

[P3]
Jeok Cheongang, who had said he was stepping away for a moment to relieve himself, returned fifteen minutes later. Something felt suspicious, and I narrowed my eyes.

[P4]
“Why are you looking at me like that?”

[P5]
“Did you really just go relieve yourself?”

[P6]
“Do you need to smell me before you’ll believe me?”

[P7]
“But it took you fifteen minutes. Could it be that—”

[P8]
“This old man has virility to spare.”

[P9]
“…”

[P10]
How virile did you have to be to spend fifteen minutes pissing?

[P11]
At that point, it wasn’t a stream. It was a fire hose.

[P12]
When I stared at him in disbelief, Jeok Cheongang glared at me.

[P13]
“What? You got a problem?”

[P14]
“Of course not.”

[P15]
A problem? Me?

[P16]
Considering all the help he had given me today, I could bow to him a hundred times and it still wouldn’t be enough.

[P17]
*And then there’s the other thing…*

[P18]
I pushed aside the thought that had suddenly occurred to me.

[P19]
The Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure. The Fire King’s Disciple.

[P20]
I also pretended not to hear the voices that had been whispering nonstop ever since.

[P21]
*Disciple? That’s ridiculous.*

[P22]
It was something I had never once considered before.

[P23]
Why would a man accept as his new Disciple someone he had known for only a day—someone who had killed the Disciple he had cherished like a son?

[P24]
*Even if that Disciple had been a colossal son of a bitch.*

[P25]
As I was thinking about it, Jin Wikyung approached and respectfully cupped his hands toward Jeok Cheongang.

[P26]
“This humble junior, Jin Wikyung, pays his respects to the Fire King Jeok Cheongang, whose fame resounds throughout the world.”

[P27]
“Are you from the Jin Family?”

[P28]
Jeok Cheongang looked Jin Wikyung up and down, then nodded as if he had figured it out.

[P29]
“Then you’re this brat’s father?”

[P30]
“What?”

[P31]
“Raise your son properly. The boy’s young, but he’s already hotheaded and causing trouble. His manners are terrible, too.”

[P32]
Jin Wikyung answered with the darkest expression I had ever seen on his face.

[P33]
“…”

[P34]
“He’s my younger brother.”

[P35]
“Hm?”

[P36]
“I’m Taekyung’s eldest brother.”

[P37]
Jeok Cheongang’s face turned serious.

[P38]
“Don’t joke around. I understand wanting to look young, but if you get too greedy, Heaven will punish you.”

[P39]
“It’s the truth. I am Jin Wikyung, the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P40]
“…”

[P41]
“How old are you, by any chance?”

[P42]
“Now that the year has turned, I’m thirty-six.”

[P43]
Jeok Cheongang muttered in disbelief.

[P44]
“You look forty-six.”

[P45]
Admittedly, his face was somewhat—quite a lot, actually—more weathered than his age suggested. Even I had mistaken him for my father at first.

[P46]
At least his hair was still thick, but there was no cure for a face that had taken a 160-kilometer-per-hour fastball from time itself.

[P47]
Seeing the sadness on Jin Wikyung’s face, Jeok Cheongang tried to comfort him.

[P48]
“It’s all right. What matters in a man is his ability. You’ve got a pretty wife and adorable children, so what more do you need? Heh heh.”

[P49]
“I’m still single.”

[P50]
“…At thirty-six?”

[P51]
In modern times, that would only be around the age when people started thinking seriously about marriage. But in Murim, where early marriage was common, thirty-six was old enough to have grandchildren.

[P52]
The bachelor Jin Wikyung gave a terse answer.

[P53]
“Yes.”

[P54]
“…”

[P55]
This silence ran a little long. The Fire King furrowed his brow, relaxed it, then flared his nostrils before finally heaving a deep sigh.

[P56]
“Damn it. I could really use a drink.”

[P57]
I let out a quiet laugh. It was a feast day, after all. What kind of feast would it be without alcohol? There was enough of it lying around to drown in.

[P58]
“Would you like a drink?”

[P59]
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened.

[P60]
“You insolent brat. Are you making fun of this old man?”

[P61]
“What?”

[P62]
“Bring me the whole crock.”

[P63]
* * *

[P64]
A mood was like a spark. Once it went out, it was difficult to rekindle.

[P65]
Yet even after the uninvited guests from the Zhongnan Sect had poured cold water over everything, the spark had not died.

[P66]
No—in the presence of the Fire King, it blazed even more fiercely.

[P67]
“Wooooo!”

[P68]
“Drink! Come on, let’s drink!”

[P69]
“I never thought I’d live to see the Fire King in person!”

[P70]
“When the Fire King gets flustered, he goes Right Fire King, Left Fire King![^1]”

[P71]
“…”

[P72]
I didn’t know who that was, but that bastard had nearly put out the spark.

[P73]
At my signal, Hyuk Mujin, who had been standing by, quietly slipped away to hunt down the mood killer.

[P74]
Meanwhile, Jeok Cheongang was receiving greetings from countless people.

[P75]
“Great Hero Jeok! It’s the honor of a lifetime to meet you!”

[P76]
“Please do us the honor of visiting our sect sometime…”

[P77]
“Please grant us your guidance!”

[P78]
It was truly a sea of people.

[P79]
The name of the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was practically synonymous with living legend.

[P80]
Moreover, his whereabouts had been unknown for decades, so most people had long accepted his death as fact.

[P81]
And now the Fire King, whom everyone had thought dead, had appeared—not in the Central Plains or on Mount Jiuhua, but right here at the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Shanxi Province.

[P82]
*Of course everyone’s going to lose their minds.*

[P83]
Perhaps this was what it would be like if the legendary singer once called the Emperor of Pop came back from the dead.

[P84]
Yet despite the enthusiasm of his local Shanxi fans, Michael Cheongang looked thoroughly displeased.

[P85]
Jin Wikyung seemed to notice, too, and sent me a Sound Transmission.

[P86]
—My youngest.

[P87]
The only people who could hold a lengthy conversation with the eccentric Jeok Cheongang were Cheongpung and me. But there was no telling where Cheongpung’s thoughts might wander, so in the end, I had no choice but to act as the messenger.

[P88]
“Are you uncomfortable?”

[P89]
“Look at the state I’m in. Wouldn’t you be uncomfortable if you were me?”

[P90]
Jeok Cheongang glared at the wine crock beside him. Quite a bit of time had passed, yet hardly any of it was gone.

[P91]
It wasn’t that he disliked alcohol. He simply hadn’t had time to drink.

[P92]
“Damn it. It shouldn’t be this hard to have a single drink.”

[P93]
People kept asking him to accept them as Disciples, while Sect Leaders and merchants begged to host him as an honored guest.

[P94]
One heavily pregnant woman had even asked if she could touch his nose. She wanted to receive the Fire King’s qi so she could give birth to a great person, or something like that.

[P95]
*Was he a dol hareubang or something?[^2]*

[P96]
It was enough to make even the onlookers snicker. How much worse must it have been for the man at the center of it all?

[P97]
Frankly, given Jeok Cheongang’s personality, the fact that he had endured this much was impressive in itself.

[P98]
“Why don’t we move somewhere I prepared in advance? It’s quiet there.”

[P99]
“Ugh. Forget it.”

[P100]
“You said you were uncomfortable.”

[P101]
“I said forget it. Why are you so damn talkative?”

[P102]
Even while grumbling, Jeok Cheongang stubbornly refused to leave. I tilted my head.

[P103]
*What’s going on?*

[P104]
We had known each other for only a short time, but I had gotten a fairly good sense of his personality.

[P105]
It was obvious that he hated noisy places and found people’s attention bothersome. That was probably why he had spent his entire life on Mount Jiuhua.

[P106]
*Then why?*

[P107]
I watched Jeok Cheongang carefully.

[P108]
In front of him, the owner of one of Shanxi Province’s most influential merchant associations was bowing and scraping.

[P109]
“Great Hero Jeok! I’ve long heard of your reputation, which shakes the entire world. When I was young, I admired you so much…”

[P110]
“Get to the point.”

[P111]
“I have always admired you from the bottom of my heart, so I prepared a small token of my sincerity.”

[P112]
“A small token?”

[P113]
“Yes. It’s something I acquired recently, but I suppose every item has its destined owner.”

[P114]
The merchant took a small wooden box from inside his robe and opened the lid. Inside was a ring set with clear jade.

[P115]
“It is a Poison-Averting Ring.”

[P116]
“A fairly valuable item. It must have been difficult to obtain.”

[P117]
The merchant waved his hands dramatically.

[P118]
“Having the honor of seeing your noble face, how could price possibly matter? It only cost a thousand silver nyang. Heh heh.”

[P119]
A thousand silver nyang for a single ring. It ranked among the most expensive gifts the Jin Family of Taiyuan had received so far.

[P120]
Jeok Cheongang, however, merely nodded without much interest.

[P121]
“Well, since you’re giving it to me, I’ll accept it gratefully. Who are you, and where are you from?”

[P122]
“I’m in charge of the Yangcheon Merchant Association…”

[P123]
“Yangcheon? That’s near Hebei.”

[P124]
The merchant had been interrupted before he could even give his name, but he bowed as if he had received a great honor.

[P125]
“Yes. We are trying to begin trading with the Hebei Peng Family, but it has not been easy.”

[P126]
That was the merchant’s real purpose.

[P127]
It was why he had sought out Jeok Cheongang even after offering a token of sincerity that was anything but small.

[P128]
In short, he wanted Jeok Cheongang to help him establish a business relationship with the Hebei Peng Family.

[P129]
“The Peng Family, huh? Who’s the Family Head these days?”

[P130]
“It is Great Hero Peng Cheolyeong, the Iron Blood Saber.”

[P131]
“I’ve never heard of him. Is he the Thunderbolt Saber King’s son?”

[P132]
“Yes, yes. The Thunderbolt Saber King retired from the front lines and passed the position of Family Head to him.”

[P133]
“This old man once had a drink with the Thunderbolt Saber King in his younger days. All right, I understand.”

[P134]
That was the end of the conversation. The merchant set down the wooden box and left with a grin stretching from ear to ear.

[P135]
Beneath the box lay a stack of bank drafts that had not been there moments ago.

[P136]
Once the merchant had withdrawn, I leaned closer and whispered to Jeok Cheongang.

[P137]
“You know the Thunderbolt Saber King?”

[P138]
As his title suggested, he was one of the Ten Kings, a Supreme Peak master just like Jeok Cheongang.

[P139]
Jeok Cheongang took a sip of wine before answering.

[P140]
“I told you. We had a drink together.”

[P141]
“Wow.”

[P142]
He talked about the Thunderbolt Saber King as if he were some old neighborhood friend. Every time he did something like this, I was reminded all over again of just how extraordinary Jeok Cheongang was.

[P143]
When I gaped at him in admiration, Jeok Cheongang puffed out his chest.

[P144]
“I flattened that bastard’s nose years ago.”

[P145]
“…What?”

[P146]
“I was having a drink with the Sword Saint when he barged in without a word and picked a fight. We fought, and I taught him a lesson.”

[P147]
What the hell was he talking about?

[P148]
“Weren’t you two friends?”

[P149]
“Me? With that guy?”

[P150]
Jeok Cheongang furrowed his brow.

[P151]
“Why would I associate with an uncultured bastard like him? We never saw each other again after that.”

[P152]
“…”

[P153]
“Later, some strange rumor even started going around. They said the Peng Family’s man and I had exchanged over a hundred moves before acknowledging each other and withdrawing. The bastards from the Hebei Peng Family must have pulled some kind of trick.”

[P154]
I was dumbfounded, and so was everyone around me.

[P155]
The story about the Thunderbolt Saber King was absurd enough, but if it was true, the merchant’s request had just gone up in smoke.

[P156]
“Th-then the Yangcheon Merchant Association won’t be able to trade with the Hebei Peng Family, will they? Mentioning Great Hero Jeok’s name will only make things worse.”

[P157]
Jeok Cheongang blinked.

[P158]
“The Yangcheon Merchant Association? What’s that?”

[P159]
“…”

[P160]
“Ah, you mean that guy from earlier? Why should I care about him?”

[P161]
“But you said you’d help him trade with the Hebei Peng Family.”

[P162]
“He asked me to meet him, so I met him. It’s also true that I had a drink with the Thunderbolt Saber King. Was there even a shred of falsehood in anything this old man said?”

[P163]
“…”

[P164]
I wasn’t sure about that, but he certainly didn’t seem to possess even a shred of conscience.

[P165]
His shamelessness was so impressive that I almost respected him for it.

[P166]
*Fire King, are you even human?*

[P167]
He had more than one or two victims. Before long, the people who had believed Jeok Cheongang’s empty promises and offered him a “small token of sincerity” would realize that it had all been complete bullshit and pound the ground in despair.

[P168]
*At this point, this is organized fraud.*

[P169]
Not that any of the victims would come forward.

[P170]
No one was brave enough to approach the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, and demand their gifts back.

[P171]
“We would be honored if you would visit our sect sometime…”

[P172]
“Hmm. I’ll stop by one day.”

[P173]
Meaning after he died and found himself wandering the netherworld.

[P174]
“This is my small token of sincerity…”

[P175]
“I’ll accept it.”

[P176]
*No. He really is just taking it.*

[P177]
As I watched the treasures, elixirs, and bank drafts pile up like a mountain, I finally realized something.

[P178]
*Was this why he stayed?*

[P179]
It was clearly part of his grand plan to make one last big haul in his old age.

[P180]
Eventually, after dealing with dozens of suckers, Jeok Cheongang spoke.

[P181]
“Hmm. This is quite a haul. Aren’t there any more?”

[P182]
Jin Wikyung answered with an exhausted expression.

[P183]
“No. It seems everyone who was likely to come has already arrived.”

[P184]
“A shame. I could have squeezed more out of them.”

[P185]
*Just look at the greed on this old man.*

[P186]
Jeok Cheongang gazed at the spoils he had earned by drinking instead of sweating, then stretched his arms high above his head.

[P187]
“Good grief, this is tiring.”

[P188]
“…”

[P189]
“Why are you looking at me like that?”

[P190]
Faced with Jeok Cheongang’s glare, I subtly averted my eyes.

[P191]
“It’s nothing. I was just admiring you.”

[P192]
“From where I’m standing, that doesn’t look like admiration.”

[P193]
“I’m serious. There’s nothing wrong with having a lot of wealth.”

[P194]
“Is that so?”

[P195]
Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh, then casually tossed out a remark.

[P196]
“Then you take it.”

[P197]
“What?”

[P198]
“I’m saying I’ll give all of it to you.”

[P199]
“All of that?”

[P200]
“It’s completely useless to this old man, but it’s different for you. Scatter it in the street or do whatever you want with it. I won’t care, so take it.”

[P201]
What was going on?

[P202]
I stared at Jeok Cheongang in bewilderment.

[P203]
*Why all of a sudden?*

[P204]
He had already helped me immensely. Naturally, I couldn’t help wondering why he was showing such extraordinary favor to both me and the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

[P205]
Could it really be what I thought? Could he truly mean it?

[P206]
I swallowed dryly and opened my mouth.

[P207]
“Great Hero Jeok, by any chance…”

[P208]
At that moment, Jeok Cheongang rose from his seat and spoke with a drunken expression.

[P209]
“Ahh, I’m drunk. I’m going inside to rest. See you tomorrow.”

[P210]
“…”

[P211]
I watched Jeok Cheongang stagger away, then turned my gaze back to the wine crock.

[P212]
The moon was reflected in the wine. He had not even emptied a quarter of the crock.

[P213]
[^1]: This puns on *jwa-wang-u-wang*, a Korean expression for being flustered or running around in confusion; *jwa* and *u* mean “left” and “right,” while *wang* means “king.”

[P214]
[^2]: A dol hareubang is a stone guardian statue from Jeju Island. Folk beliefs associate touching its nose with fertility.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 194

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃194화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“아따, 시원하다.”
  6|
  7|잠시 소피를 보고 온다던 적천강이 돌아온 것은 일각이 지난 후였다. 어쩐지 수상쩍은 느낌에 나는 눈을 가늘게 떴다.
  8|
  9|“눈을 왜 그따위로 뜨느냐?”
 10|
 11|“정말 소피보고 오신 거 맞아요?”
 12|
 13|“냄새라도 맡아 봐야 믿겠느냐?”
 14|
 15|“일각이나 걸리셨는데. 혹시.”
 16|
 17|“노부가 한 정력 하느니라.”
 18|
 19|“…….”
 20|
 21|대체 얼마나 정력이 좋으면 소변을 15분이나 보는 거야.
 22|
 23|그 정도면 소변이 아니라 소방 호스 아닌가. 내가 어이없단 표정으로 바라보자 적천강이 눈을 치켜떴다.
 24|
 25|“뭐, 불만 있어?”
 26|
 27|“그럴 리가요.”
 28|
 29|불만이라니.
 30|
 31|오늘 그에게 받은 도움을 생각하면 백 번을 절해도 부족하다.
 32|
 33|‘그리고 또…….’
 34|
 35|문득 떠오르는 생각을 흩어 버렸다.
 36|
 37|열화문의 신물, 화왕의 제자. 아까부터 끊임없이 수군거리는 목소리들도 애써 못 들은 척했다.
 38|
 39|‘제자라니, 말도 안 되는 소리.’
 40|
 41|지금까지 단 한 번도 생각해 본 적 없는 문제였다.
 42|
 43|애초에 만난 지 하루 된, 그것도 자식처럼 끔찍이 아끼던 제자를 죽인 놈을 새로운 제자로 받아들일 이유가 어디 있겠는가.
 44|
 45|‘비록 그 제자가 천하의 개썅놈이라도 말이지.’
 46|
 47|그런 생각을 하고 있을 때, 진위경이 다가와 적천강에게 지극히 공손한 태도로 포권을 취했다.
 48|
 49|“무림 말학 진위경이 천하에 위명이 자자하신 화왕 적천강 대협을 뵙습니다.”
 50|
 51|“진가?”
 52|
 53|진위경을 위아래로 스캔한 적천강이 감 잡았다는 듯 고개를 끄덕였다.
 54|
 55|“하면 자네가 이놈 애비 되는 사람인가?”
 56|
 57|“예?”
 58|
 59|“자식 교육 좀 똑바로 시키게. 어린놈이 벌써부터 욱해서 사고나 치고 다니고 말이야. 말투도 영 싸가지가 없어.”
 60|
 61|진위경이 지금까지 본 가장 어두운 얼굴로 대답했다.
 62|
 63|“……제 아우입니다.”
 64|
 65|“응?”
 66|
 67|“제가 태경이 큰형 되는 사람입니다.”
 68|
 69|적천강이 정색했다.
 70|
 71|“농담하지 말게. 젊어 보이고 싶은 마음은 알지만 욕심이 너무 과하면 천벌 받아.”
 72|
 73|“사실입니다. 태원진가의 소가주 진위경이 바로 접니다.”
 74|
 75|“……혹시 나이가 어떻게 되나?”
 76|
 77|“해가 바뀌었으니 올해로 서른여섯입니다.”
 78|
 79|적천강이 불신의 눈빛으로 중얼거렸다.
 80|
 81|“마흔 여섯은 되어 보이는데.”
 82|
 83|나이에 비해 좀, 상당히, 많이 삭은 얼굴이긴 하지. 처음에는 나도 아버지로 착각했을 정도니까.
 84|
 85|그나마 머리카락은 풍성한데, 세월을 160km 패스트볼로 맞은 얼굴은 해결책이 안 보인다.
 86|
 87|슬픔에 잠긴 진위경의 표정에 적천강이 애써 위로했다.
 88|
 89|“괜찮아. 사내는 능력일세. 예쁜 색시에 귀여운 자식 놈들이 있으니 됐지 뭘. 허허.”
 90|
 91|“아직 홀몸입니다.”
 92|
 93|“……서른여섯인데?”
 94|
 95|현대에서야 슬슬 결혼 생각할 나이지만 조혼(早婚)이 흔한 무림에서는 서른여섯이면 손자도 볼 수 있는 나이다.
 96|
 97|싱글남 진위경이 짧게 대답했다.
 98|
 99|“예.”
100|
101|“…….”
102|
103|이번 침묵을 좀 길다. 미간을 찡그렸다가, 폈다가. 콧구멍을 벌름거리던 화왕이 한숨을 푹 내쉬었다.
104|
105|“젠장, 술 땡기네.”
106|
107|나는 피식 웃었다. 오늘 같은 잔칫날에 술이 빠져서야 쓰나, 주위에 널리고 널린 게 술이다.
108|
109|“한 잔 드려요?”
110|
111|내 말에 적천강이 눈을 동그랗게 떴다.
112|
113|“이런 되바라진 놈을 봤나. 지금 노부랑 장난하는 것이냐?”
114|
115|“예?”
116|
117|“동이째로 가져오너라.”
118|
119|
120|
121|* * *
122|
123|
124|
125|원래 분위기라는 것은 불씨 같아서, 한 번 꺼지면 다시 타오르기 힘들다. 하지만 종남파의 불청객들이 찬물을 뿌리고 난 후에도 불씨는 죽지 않았다.
126|
127|아니, 화왕이라는 존재로 인해 더욱 거세게 타올랐다.
128|
129|“우와아아아!”
130|
131|“마셔! 마시자고!”
132|
133|“내가 살면서 화왕을 직접 보게 될 줄이야.”
134|
135|“화왕이 당황하면 우화왕 좌화왕!”
136|
137|“…….”
138|
139|누군지는 모르지만 방금 저 새끼가 불씨 꺼트릴 뻔했네.
140|
141|내 눈짓에 대기하고 있던 혁무진이 분위기 살인마를 색출하기 위해 슬그머니 자리를 떴다.
142|
143|그사이 적천강은 수많은 사람의 인사를 받고 있었다.
144|
145|“적 대협! 이렇게 뵙게 되어 일생의 영광입니다!”
146|
147|“추후에 꼭 저희 문파에 들러 주시면…….”
148|
149|“가르침을 내려 주십시오!”
150|
151|말 그대로 인산인해.
152|
153|화왕 적천강이라는 이름은 살아 있는 전설이나 다름없다.
154|
155|더군다나 수십 년간 행적이 묘연한 탓에 대부분의 사람들은 그의 죽음을 공공연한 사실로 받아들이고 있었다.
156|
157|그런데 죽은 줄 알았던 화왕이 나타난 것이다. 중원도, 구화산도 아닌 바로 이곳 산서성의 태원진가에.
158|
159|‘난리가 날 수밖에 없지.’
160|
161|팝의 황제라 불리던 전설적인 가수가 살아 돌아온다면 이 정도일까 싶다.
162|
163|하지만 산서성 현지 팬들의 성원에도 불구하고 마이클 천강은 영 떨떠름한 얼굴이었다.
164|
165|진위경도 그런 낌새를 느꼈는지 전음을 보냈다.
166|
167|- 막내야.
168|
169|괴팍한 성격인 적천강과 그나마 길게 말을 섞을 수 있는 사람은 나와 청풍밖에 없는데, 청풍은 어디로 튈지 모르는 놈이라 결국 내가 메신저 역할을 할 수밖에 없었다.
170|
171|“불편한 곳이라도 있으세요?”
172|
173|“노부의 꼴을 봐라. 네 녀석 같으면 안 불편하겠느냐?”
174|
175|적천강이 옆에 놓인 술동이를 노려봤다. 시간이 꽤 흘렀는데도 얼마 비워지지 않은 상태였다.
176|
177|술을 싫어하는 것이 아니라 그만큼 마실 틈이 부족했던 거다.
178|
179|“염병할. 술 한 잔 마시기가 이렇게 힘들어서야.”
180|
181|다짜고짜 제자로 받아 달라는 사람, 귀빈으로 모시고 싶다는 문주들과 상인들.
182|
183|심지어 어떤 만삭의 여인은 코를 만져 봐도 되냐고 묻기까지 했다. 화왕의 기운을 받아 큰 인물을 낳고 싶다나 뭐라나.
184|
185|‘돌하르방인가.’
186|
187|보는 사람도 실소가 새어 나올 정도인데 당사자는 오죽할까.
188|
189|사실 적천강의 성격에 이 정도 버틴 것만 해도 대단한 거다.
190|
191|“그럼 미리 준비해 둔 곳으로 자리를 옮길까요? 거긴 조용한데.”
192|
193|“끄응. 됐다.”
194|
195|“불편하시다면서요.”
196|
197|“아, 됐다면 된 거지 왜 이렇게 말이 많아?”
198|
199|투덜거리면서도 끝끝내 자리를 뜨지 않는 적천강의 모습에 나는 고개를 갸우뚱했다.
200|
201|‘뭐지?’
202|
203|만난 시간은 짧지만 그의 성격은 어느 정도 알고 있다.
204|
205|시끄러운 곳 싫어하고 사람들의 관심을 귀찮아하는 게 눈에 보일 정도다. 애초에 그런 성격이니 일평생을 구화산에서 살았던 것이고.
206|
207|‘그런데 왜?’
208|
209|나는 유심히 적천강의 모습을 살폈다.
210|
211|그의 앞에는 산서성에서 방귀깨나 뀐다는 상회(商會)의 주인이 허리를 굽실거리고 있었다.
212|
213|“아이고! 적천강 대협! 천하를 떨어 울리는 위명은 익히 들었습니다. 제가 어릴 때 얼마나 대협을…….”
214|
215|“본론만 말하게.”
216|
217|“평소 마음 깊이 대협을 흠모하던 터라 약소한 성의를 준비했습니다.”
218|
219|“약소한 성의?”
220|
221|“예. 얼마 전에 얻은 물건이온데, 역시 주인을 따로 있나 봅니다.”
222|
223|품에서 작은 목함을 꺼낸 상인이 뚜껑을 열었다. 투명한 옥이 박힌 반지가 모습을 드러냈다.
224|
225|“피독지환(避毒指環)입니다.”
226|
227|“제법 귀한 물건이군. 구하기 힘들었을 터인데?”
228|
229|상인이 과장스럽게 손을 내저었다.
230|
231|“적 대협의 존안을 뵙게 되었는데 가격이 문제겠습니까! 은자 천 냥 정도밖에 안 합니다. 헤헤.”
232|
233|저런 반지 하나가 은자 천 냥이라니. 지금까지 태원진가에 들어온 예물 중에서도 손에 꼽는 가격이다.
234|
235|하지만 적천강은 별 감흥 없는 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였다.
236|
237|“뭐, 일단 주니까 고맙게 받지. 어디에서 온 누구라고?”
238|
239|“양천상회를 맡고 있는…….”
240|

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
